utterances.text: The window of that office faces the Drina River, not the road. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 13th, when you told us about this brief meeting with Jasikovac, when you called him back from the ambushes, Sreten Milosevic was your operational duty officer then, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Sreten Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on the 14th, that you learned that, at 1400 hours, that a large number of prisoners were being brought to the Zvornik area from Major Zoran Jovanovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that when the reinforcements arrived a little after 1400 hours, or 1400 hours, those reinforcements were brought in by Major Zoran Jovanovic. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Jovanovic is the head of the military police; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right. Mr. Jovanovic, a major, was I think -- well, I don't know the exact post he held in the brigade command, but he worked in the staff office, different things with respect to the computer. The head of the military police was Jasikovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I did get those two confused. That's my fault. You said after the 14th, in the morning of the 14th, that you left the intersection at Snagovo and went to the headquarters, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 14th? No. That's not what I said. I didn't go to the headquarters on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Dragan Jevtic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Dragan Jevtic is, if you mean his military post at the time, was commander of the engineers company. Otherwise, he was a citizen living in Zvornik, and he was a graduate of architecture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was commander of the engineering company, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. You're quite right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have a lot of respect for him; you think he is a bright and respectable man, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you want me to state publicly here and now, then I can say that he's a well-educated man. I think he's a clever man, able to do his job. I don't think it's only me who respects him. Anybody who knows him we will probably respects him too, like everybody else who is a good person and well educated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your direct testimony you described the burial of 20 or so Muslim soldiers by the Zvornik Brigade, in the name of terrain restoration, after a combat operation. Although this is the normal responsibility of the logistics company, the civilian protection organisation participated in that burial operation, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I put it that way. What happened was, after the fighting there in the Baljkovica area, there were some 20 corpses, or however many, which were found, and the soldiers belonging to units who were deployed there gathered up the bodies, and the 4th Battalion had already arrived from Bratunac, which was renamed the 8th Battalion. And the burial itself was done by the machinery from the engineers company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't remember a man named Kosta Eric participating in this burial operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. Our brigade was a large one. There were 50 companies to the brigade, 11 battalions, and if you expect me to know each and every soldier, well, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the burial of combat fatalities is a standard operating procedure for a military brigade, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to go to the transcript from October 2nd, and I believe there is some dispute as to whether this was considered a top-secret military operation. But I would like to go through your testimony on the reburials. First of all, you said that the people that came from Main Staff came and operated in civilian clothes; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as that is concerned, I mentioned Colonel Beara and Popovic, and I said that they came, according to what I heard later, and that at the time they were wearing civilian clothes. I don't recall having mentioned anybody else from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that all of the traffic was stopped along the way during that time by the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite sure I said that what I had heard with respect to that was that some unit from the corps battalion of the military police of the Drina Corps was blocking the roads, the communication lines, via which the loaded-up trucks with the corpses of the people to be reburied were moving along, and it was them that did that, according to what I had heard. The military police of the Drina Corps, or one of its units, at least. Now, whether the MUP had taken part, I don't know. Perhaps it did. I didn't hear anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they went so far to cover this up as to change truck drivers in midstream so that nobody knew what they were doing or where they were going, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard. That was the story going round, and I think it's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to go now to -- you admitted that you were the commander responsible for all the operations at the Zvornik Brigade on the 14th and 15th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that as the chief of staff and also the deputy of the battalion commander, that I was in command of the units of the Zvornik Brigade which were in the Zvornik area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to provide for the witness, and copies for everybody, a copy of what is marked for identification purposes as D10/3. I have a B/C/S version here. Thank you. Do you have a copy of it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document is from the federal secretariat for National Defence, brigade rules; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photocopy of the first two pages. The title page, brigade rules, and the page after that, Articles 117 to 123 of the said rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. And if you'd like a full copy of the rules of the brigade, we could provide it to you, but I was just going to refer to one paragraph, and that is paragraph 120. "Organs for combat arms are specialised organs of the command which recommend the most appropriate use of units of each combat arm, so the brigade as a whole can fulfil its assignment in the best way. They recommend measures and activities to be completed by all brigade units." And then it lists engineers, security, anti-aircraft, anti-nuclear, chemical, and biological measures, and suchlike, within their combat arms, for the assignment to be carried out to the greatest possible effect. This is in relation to the top sentence up there, says what chiefs are responsible for. Now, the chief of operation is used to recommend the most appropriate use. He's like an expert. He makes recommendations to the commander or the deputy commander, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the chief for operative and -- operations and training organs?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The chief of any organ. You have the chief of security, you have the chief of engineering, you have the chief of whatever else you have. It's referring to the chiefs. Their duties are to propose ideas to the commander, and the commander makes the decision based on the information given by the expert organ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, but with this proviso: We have to define the chief of security, what that is, and some of these other duties that you mentioned. It's not -- they're not in the headquarters, the command. The chiefs of the services, the branches, PVO, artillery, communications, they are in the staff at the headquarters, and within the frameworks of their branch, yes, they propose to the commander the best possible use of the forces and equipment available from their sector: The artilleryman with respect to the artillery, the communications man with respect to the communications, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you're aware that on July 14th through the morning of the 15th, Dragan Jokic wore two hats, so we say: He was chief of engineering and he was also assigned as duty officer on that day; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to clear up: In your direct testimony, on page 2443 of the transcript, you stated that Dragan Jokic was chief of staff, and I think maybe that was a misinterpretation. Dragan Jokic was never chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade, was he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was recorded and what was interpreted, but I don't think I said that. The chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade was myself. I was. And also deputy commander when the commander was absent, I automatically took over his duties and became the commander, or rather, I was the deputy. So I have absolutely no intention of saying that Jokic was chief of staff when he wasn't. I was chief of staff, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the question is misleading in that I believe there was a question on that point regarding 1992, in the early days of the brigade, is my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, no matter what the situation, the witness has answered this question in a proper way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I think the question was confusing, and I'm not sure the witness understood it because of the confusion. But ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'll ask him a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, if there's any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, you have worked with Mr. Jokic in the JNA, and then when it was transformed into the VRS, and I just wanted, as far as your knowledge goes, Dragan Jokic has never been chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade, has he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Jokic was a major. He was chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade during two periods. At the beginning, when it was first formed. So when I came, provisionally, on the 15th of June, I found him there as chief of staff. Then temporarily, for one month, I performed those functions and he was appointed commander of some training centre. And then once again, when I came on the 1st of December to the VRS, then Major Jokic was chief of staff on that occasion as well. After that, however, he became head of the engineers and I was the chief of staff. So during those two periods - and I think you'll be able to find it in the papers relating to the personnel department - Dragan Jokic was indeed the chief of staff. I thought you meant with respect to your first question that you were asking for the July period, July 1995. That's why my answer was as it was, that I was the chief of staff in 1995., except for the time that I was deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I thank you for clearing that up for me, because I was never aware that he was ever chief of staff. And when you talk about that transition period when he may have been chief of staff at one time, are you talking about for a temporary one-week period or just until somebody was substituted in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a misstatement of the testimony. He never said "may have."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, I believe that the counsel has the right to ask this question, to make these things clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To sum up, if you look at it time-wise, with respect to the period, if I remember correctly, the first half of June 1992, and then later on, from about the 20th of July, or, to try and be even more precise from the end of July 1992 until the 1st of December 1992. So during that time Major Jokic was chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade. I don't know whether he was appointed to that post or whether he was the acting chief of staff, but anyway, he was there doing the job. Now, after the 1st of December, when I arrived, I continued to occupy that post. I took up the post. Of course, it wasn't our own choice. We were following orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for clearing that up for us. As duty officer and chief of engineering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, it's time to break, you know. We have been sitting here for a long time. Maybe you could continue your cross tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of October 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
